meta.title: The Rocket and the Orbit
meta.skill_frame: Use a fact from an earlier part to answer a question about a later one.

reader.who: High school students who read at about a 5th-grade level.
reader.why_this_level: Flesch-Kincaid on the three parts together is about 6.7. The two-step chain from the lock lesson stays. The new load is clue distance: the rocket fact is in the first part, and Glenn's flight is in the second. Three people, two rockets, and the animal flights. This is a grade-5 instructional lesson, stage 1, and this sequence is retry text.
reader.tone: Adult subject. Plain sentences. The lesson must not make the reader feel small.

source.attribution: National Aeronautics and Space Administration, NASA STEM Team, 'What Was Project Mercury? source.survey: Three stretches of the NASA STEM Team article, in source order. The word list, the mission table, one sentence about Shepard's later moon flight, the astronauts after Glenn, and the closing sentence that says the animal flights proved it was safe were left out. No kept sentence was rewritten.
source.avoided: The grades 5-8 John Glenn biography measured FK 4.38, under the band floor, and was not used. The longer Glenn history page measured about FK 11.9.

session.difficulty_basis: Clue distance. The inference is still a two-step chain, and one other rocket can still look like the answer. The new load is that the two facts sit in different parts.

authoring_exceptions: Advance and retry both name inference_band_5_1_0006, the next lesson in this stage.
One sentence about Shepard's later Apollo flight is omitted from the middle of that paragraph so the part stays on the Mercury flights.

script_overrides.near_copy_2: Start with the rocket, or with the orbit. One sentence is enough.

passage.part_1:
The Mercury spacecraft was designed for this project. It was a small capsule with room for one astronaut. The astronaut stayed in his seat during the flight.

Two types of rockets were used for Project Mercury. The first two of the six flights with an astronaut on board used a Redstone rocket. The four manned flights that orbited Earth used an Atlas rocket. Both of these rockets were originally designed as missiles for the United States military.

The project was named Mercury after a Roman god who was very fast. Each astronaut named his spacecraft. Alan Shepard included a 7 in the name of his Mercury capsule. This was because it was the seventh one made. The other astronauts included a 7 also. This was in honor of the seven astronauts chosen for the project.
passage.part_2:
NASA selected seven astronauts for Project Mercury in 1959. Choosing the astronauts was one of the first things NASA did. The agency was only six months old when it chose them.

Alan Shepard made the first Mercury flight. That flight made him the first American in space. The 15-minute flight went into space and came back down. His Mercury capsule was named Freedom 7.

Gus Grissom was the second astronaut to fly in Project Mercury. Grissom named his capsule Liberty Bell 7. The third astronaut to fly in Project Mercury was John Glenn. In 1962, he became the first American to orbit Earth, aboard Friendship 7.
passage.part_3:
Before astronauts flew in Project Mercury, NASA conducted several test flights. These launches did not have people aboard. The test flights helped NASA find and fix problems.

The first Atlas rocket launched with a Mercury capsule exploded. The first Mercury-Redstone launch only went about four inches off the ground. From these flights, NASA learned how to fix the rockets and make them safer.

Three other "astronauts" also helped make sure Mercury was safer. A rhesus monkey, Sam, and two chimpanzees, Ham and Enos, flew in Mercury capsules. Sam and Ham made suborbital flights. Sam flew on a "Little Joe" rocket. Ham flew on a Redstone rocket. Enos launched on an Atlas rocket. He made two orbits around Earth.

items.prompt: The first two flights with a person aboard came back down. Which rocket flew the trips that orbited Earth?

tutor_only.confirm: Right. The flights that orbited Earth used an Atlas rocket.
tutor_only.correct_reason: The passage says the first two crewed flights used a Redstone, and the four flights that orbited Earth used an Atlas.
tutor_only.core_idea: The flights that orbited Earth used an Atlas rocket.
accept_ideas: Atlas. Those were the flights that orbited.

partial.when: They say a rocket, or both rockets, and they do not name Atlas or Redstone.
partial.ask: Two rockets are named. Which one flew the trips that orbited?

if_they_say.when: They say the Redstone, or that both rockets orbited.
if_they_say.ask: The Redstone flew the first two flights. Those came back down. Which rocket orbited?

if_they_say.when: They say the number 7, or the name of a capsule.
if_they_say.ask: The 7 is in the capsule names. The question is about the rocket. Which one orbited?

help: Find the sentence that names the four flights that orbited Earth.
Which rocket does that sentence give?
tutor_only.tell: The first two crewed flights used a Redstone and came back down. The four flights that orbited Earth used an Atlas.

items.prompt: Both rockets were first built as missiles. What job were they built for before they carried an astronaut?

tutor_only.confirm: Right. They were built for the military, not as a ride for an astronaut.
tutor_only.correct_reason: The passage says both rockets were originally designed as missiles for the United States military. The capsule, not the rockets, was designed for this project.
tutor_only.core_idea: They were built first as military missiles, not to carry an astronaut.
accept_ideas: They were weapons first, not passenger rockets.
A military job. Carrying an astronaut came later.

partial.when: They say missiles, and they do not say military or that the first job was not carrying a person.
partial.ask: Missile is the word. Who were those missiles for, before an astronaut rode one?

if_they_say.when: They say the rockets were built to carry astronauts, or for Project Mercury.
if_they_say.ask: The capsule was designed for this project. The sentence about the rockets says they were designed as something else. What?

help: Find the sentence that starts with Both of these rockets.
It says what they were originally designed as, and for whom.
tutor_only.tell: Both rockets were originally designed as missiles for the military. Carrying an astronaut was not the job they were built for first.

items.prompt: Shepard's flight went into space and came back down. What was new about Glenn's flight?

tutor_only.confirm: Right. Glenn was the first American to orbit Earth. Shepard's flight did not orbit.
tutor_only.correct_reason: Shepard was the first American in space, on a 15-minute flight that came back down. Glenn, in 1962, was the first American to orbit Earth.
tutor_only.core_idea: Glenn's flight orbited Earth. Shepard's flight did not.
accept_ideas: He was the first American to orbit Earth.
Glenn went around Earth. Shepard only went up and came down.
Orbiting was the new part. Being in space was not.

partial.when: They say Glenn flew, or name Friendship 7, and they do not say orbit.
partial.ask: He did fly. What did his flight do that Shepard's 15-minute flight did not?

if_they_say.when: They say Glenn was the first American in space.
if_they_say.ask: That description belongs to Shepard. Glenn's sentence uses a different word than in space. What is it?

if_they_say.when: They say Grissom was first, or that Glenn was the second flier.
if_they_say.ask: Grissom flew second. The passage gives Glenn a first of his own. What was it?

help: Shepard's flight came back down. Find the sentence about Glenn in 1962.
What does that sentence say he was the first American to do?
tutor_only.tell: Shepard was first in space, and his flight came back down. Glenn was the first American to orbit Earth.

items.prompt: The first Atlas launch exploded, and the first Redstone rose about four inches. Why were no people aboard?

tutor_only.confirm: Right. Those flights were tests. NASA was still finding and fixing problems.
tutor_only.correct_reason: The passage says the launches had no people aboard and that the test flights helped NASA find and fix problems. The explosion and the four-inch launch are the problems.
tutor_only.core_idea: They were tests so NASA could find and fix problems before a person flew.
accept_ideas: NASA was testing the rockets and fixing what failed.
A person was not aboard because the rockets still had problems.
They were empty tests. One blew up and one barely rose.

partial.when: They name the explosion or the four inches, and they do not say why no person was aboard.
partial.ask: Those are the failures. Why run them with no one inside?

if_they_say.when: They say the animals were aboard those two launches.
if_they_say.ask: Sam, Ham, and Enos come later. These two launches are described before that. Who was not aboard?

if_they_say.when: They say the rockets were missiles, so they were meant to explode.
if_they_say.ask: They had been missiles. This part gives a different reason for the empty launches. What was NASA trying to find?

help: The passage says these launches did not have people aboard.
The next sentence says what the test flights helped NASA do. What was it?
tutor_only.tell: No one was aboard those launches. They were tests, and NASA used them to find and fix problems before a person flew.

items.prompt: Glenn's flight orbited Earth. Which rocket fits that kind of flight, and what was that rocket first built as?

tutor_only.confirm: Right. An Atlas. It was first built as a military missile.
tutor_only.correct_reason: Part 1 says the flights that orbited Earth used an Atlas, and that both rockets were originally missiles for the military. Part 2 says Glenn's flight orbited Earth.
tutor_only.core_idea: An Atlas rocket, first built as a military missile.
accept_ideas: The Atlas, and it was first a missile for the military.
Atlas. Both rockets started as military missiles.
An Atlas rocket, originally a missile.

partial.when: They say Atlas, or the orbiting rocket, and they do not say missile or military.
partial.ask: Atlas is the rocket. The first part also says what both rockets were built as before Mercury. What was that?

partial.when: They say a missile, or the military, and they do not name Atlas or Redstone.
partial.ask: That is the first job. Which of the two rockets flew the trips that orbited, like Glenn's?

if_they_say.when: They say the Redstone, including a Redstone that was also a missile.
if_they_say.ask: The Redstone flew the flights that came back down. Glenn orbited. Which rocket flew that kind of trip?

if_they_say.when: They say the number 7, Little Joe, or only Enos.
if_they_say.ask: Enos did orbit on an Atlas. The question asks which rocket fits Glenn's kind of flight, and what that rocket was first built as.

help: Glenn orbited. Which sentence names the rocket for flights that orbited Earth?
The same part says what both rockets were originally designed as. What was it?
tutor_only.tell: Glenn orbited, and the flights that orbited used an Atlas. That rocket, like the Redstone, was first built as a military missile.
